s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive umbilical discomfort with a firm, ulcerated nodule and associated abdominal mass
salient_findings: Firm, ulcerated nodule at the umbilicus
Poorly defined, firm mass in the right hypochondrium
key_facts: 55-year-old man with no significant medical history
10-month history of spontaneous, progressively painful umbilical discomfort
Firm nodule at the umbilicus that gradually increased in size and became ulcerated and tender
Umbilical lesion measured 6 cm by 6 cm and bled on contact
Deep palpation of the abdomen revealed a poorly defined, firm mass approximately 8 cm in diameter in the right hypochondrium
Biopsy of the umbilical lesion demonstrated a well-differentiated, infiltrating adenocarcinoma
Contrast-enhanced abdominal CT showed homogeneously enhancing umbilical tissue growth
Irregular, circumferential thickening of the right third of the transverse colon measuring approximately 8.3 cm
Total colonoscopy revealed no endoluminal lesion
